mechanism: Potentiates GABA-A receptor chloride currents, producing dose-dependent CNS depression.
preparation: Lipid emulsion (soybean oil/egg lecithin/glycerol) — supports microbial growth once opened.
dilution: Usually given undiluted for bolus; for infusion may be used neat via dedicated line/pump.

pharmacokinetics.onset: ~30–45 seconds (loss of consciousness within ~1 min of induction dose)
pharmacokinetics.duration: 5–10 minutes (single bolus); context-sensitive half-time prolonged with infusion
pharmacokinetics.halfLife: Terminal half-life hours; clinical offset fast due to redistribution

adult.label: Induction
adult.value: 1–2.5 mg/kg IV; dose reduced with increasing age (elderly >60 yr often 1–1.75 mg/kg, especially with premedication)
adult.notes: Physiologic determinants of induction dose: age, lean body mass, central blood volume. Opiate/benzodiazepine premedication markedly reduces requirement.

pediatric.label: Induction (>1 month)
pediatric.value: ED95 2–3 mg/kg; children require larger mg/kg than adults
pediatric.notes: Not for procedural sedation in children <16 yr in ICU (PRIS risk).

geriatric.label: Induction
geriatric.value: Reduce dose ~20–50%; patients >80 yr may need ~half the young-adult dose
geriatric.notes: Older/sicker (ASA III–IV) patients develop more profound hypotension, especially combined with an opiate.

obese.label: Induction
obese.value: Commonly dosed on lean/adjusted body weight

infusion.label: TIVA maintenance
infusion.value: 50–150 mcg/kg/min IV combined with N2O or an opiate; after induction, 100–200 mcg/kg/min usually needed, titrated to stimulus
infusion.notes: Sedation 25–75 mcg/kg/min; antiemetic 10–20 mg IV (can repeat q5–10 min) — propofol has intrinsic antiemetic activity.

maximum.label: Infusion duration caution
maximum.value: Prolonged high-dose infusion carries Propofol Infusion Syndrome (PRIS) risk

pregnancy: Crosses placenta; used for GA in pregnancy when indicated — institutional protocol should guide use.
lactation: Considered compatible in many protocols; confirm locally.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to propofol or its emulsion components (soy/egg allergy — verify institutional stance)
interactions: Synergistic CNS/respiratory depression with opioids and benzodiazepines
overdoseManagement: Supportive: airway, ventilation, vasopressor support for hypotension.
storage: Store per manufacturer instructions; discard opened vial within manufacturer-specified window (lipid emulsion supports bacterial growth).
quickTips: Injection pain reduced by pre-treatment with IV lidocaine or injecting into a larger vein
Reduce dose in elderly and when co-inducting with opioids

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 21 Intravenous Anesthetics)

rsi.label: RSI induction
rsi.notes: Commonly paired with rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg for RSI.

infusionPrep: TIVA: 200 mg in 20 mL (or 500 mg in 50 mL NS) → 10 mg/mL; run 50–150 mcg/kg/min.
fluidCompatibility: Lipid emulsion — give via dedicated line; do not mix with other agents in the same syringe.

mechanism: Depolarises the neuromuscular junction as an acetylcholine receptor agonist, resistant to acetylcholinesterase; produces fasciculation then paralysis.

pharmacokinetics.onset: ~30–60 seconds (ED95 ~1 mg/kg; 1 mg/kg gives intubating conditions in ~60 s)
pharmacokinetics.duration: ~5–10 minutes (metabolism by plasma cholinesterase; prolonged in deficiency)

adult.label: RSI / intubation dose
adult.value: 1–1.5 mg/kg IV (ED95 ~1 mg/kg; 1.5 mg/kg commonly used for rapid sequence induction)

pediatric.label: RSI dose
pediatric.value: Commonly higher mg/kg than adults; confirm institutional pediatric protocol

emergency.label: RSI / difficult airway
emergency.value: 1.5 mg/kg IV commonly used for rapid sequence induction

maximum.label: IM route (no IV access)
maximum.value: Up to ~4 mg/kg IM (slower onset) — confirm local protocol

contraindications: Hyperkalaemia risk states (burns >24h old, denervation injury, prolonged immobility, crush injury, massive trauma)
Personal/family history of pseudocholinesterase deficiency without safeguards
Known acute myocardial infarction / serious dysrhythmias (relative — hyperkalaemia/arrhythmia risk)
interactions: Prolonged block with anticholinesterases, some chemotherapy agents affecting pseudocholinesterase
sideEffects: Trigger for malignant hyperthermia in susceptible individuals
overdoseManagement: Supportive ventilation until block resolves (plasma cholinesterase regenerates); manage hyperkalaemia if it occurs; treat as MH if triggered (see Crisis Management module).
ampouleColor: Convention varies by manufacturer — always read the label
quickTips: Pre-treatment/atropine considered in children and for repeat dosing due to bradycardia risk
Avoid in uncontrolled hyperkalaemia and rhabdomyolysis-risk states

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 24 Pharmacology of Neuromuscular Blocking Drugs and Antagonists)

rsi.label: RSI paralytic
rsi.notes: Intubating conditions in ~60 s; avoid in uncontrolled hyperkalaemia / MH risk.

pediatricRsi.label: RSI (no IV access)
pediatricRsi.notes: Slower onset than IV; use when IV access delayed.

fluidCompatibility: Reconstitute with water for injection; do not refrigerate reconstituted solution.

mechanism: Alpha-1 (vasoconstriction), beta-1 (inotropy/chronotropy), beta-2 (bronchodilation) agonism.
dilution: 1 mg in 10 mL = 1:10,000 (100 mcg/mL) for IV cardiac arrest / anaphylaxis IV titration.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Immediate (IV)

adult.label: Anaphylaxis (IM)
adult.value: 0.5 mg (0.5 mL of 1:1000) IM, anterolateral thigh, may repeat every 5–15 min

pediatric.label: Anaphylaxis (IM)
pediatric.value: 0.01 mg/kg IM of 1:1000 (max 0.5 mg per dose) — confirm local protocol

infusion.label: Push-dose pressor (peri-arrest hypotension)
infusion.value: Highly protocol-dependent (commonly 5–20 mcg IV boluses of a 10 mcg/mL dilution) — confirm institutional push-dose protocol before use

contraindications: None absolute in true anaphylaxis or cardiac arrest
interactions: Caution with non-selective beta-blockade (unopposed alpha effect)
ampouleColor: Per ISA/AHA crash-cart colour convention — confirm your institution's crash cart labelling
quickTips: Confirm concentration (1:1000 vs 1:10,000) before every draw — a frequent source of 10x dosing error

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (ACLS-aligned teaching doses)

infusionPrep: Push-dose: 1 mg in 100 mL NS → 10 mcg/mL; give 5–20 mcg IV boluses. Infusion: 1 mg in 250 mL NS → 4 mcg/mL (titrate).
fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS; absorbed by some plastics — use dedicated line for infusions.

mechanism: Competitive antagonism at muscarinic acetylcholine receptors.
concentrations: 0.6 mg/mL (commonly available Indian ampoule strength — check label)

pharmacokinetics.onset: Rapid (IV)

adult.label: Symptomatic bradycardia
adult.value: 0.5 mg IV every 3–5 min, max 3 mg total (ACLS teaching value)

pediatric.label: Bradycardia
pediatric.value: 0.02 mg/kg IV (minimum dose conventions vary) — confirm institutional pediatric protocol

emergency.label: Organophosphate poisoning
emergency.value: Doses are much higher and titrated to secretions — specialist/toxicology-guided, not covered by this seed entry

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Standard ACLS teaching doses)

fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS; mix with neostigmine for reversal.

mechanism: Blocks 5-HT3 receptors centrally (chemoreceptor trigger zone) and peripherally (vagal afferents).

pharmacokinetics.onset: Minutes (IV)

adult.label: PONV prophylaxis
adult.value: 4 mg IV, typically near end of surgery (Miller's: 4 mg IV ~30 min before conclusion of surgery)
adult.notes: Part of multimodal PONV prophylaxis (combine with a steroid such as dexamethasone).

pediatric.label: PONV prophylaxis
pediatric.value: 0.1 mg/kg IV (commonly max 4 mg) — confirm institutional protocol

interactions: Additive QT prolongation with other QT-prolonging drugs
monitoring: ECG if other QT-prolonging risk factors present

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 76 Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting; Ch. 21)

infusionPrep: Infusion (if used): 4 mg in 50 mL NS → 80 mcg/mL; run over 15–30 min.
fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS/RL.

drugClass: Amide local anaesthetic / Class Ib antiarrhythmic
mechanism: Blocks voltage-gated sodium channels, reducing nerve conduction.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Fast

adult.label: Max dose, plain
adult.value: ~4.5 mg/kg (commonly quoted ceiling ~300 mg)
adult.notes: With epinephrine, plain-tissue ceiling rises toward ~7 mg/kg.

maximum.label: Max dose, with adrenaline
maximum.notes: Reduce in small patients, extremes of age, cardiac/hepatic disease, and when injecting into vascular/High-uptake sites.

sideEffects: Local Anaesthetic Systemic Toxicity (LAST) — see Crisis Management module
overdoseManagement: Follow LAST protocol (airway support, seizure control, IV lipid emulsion) — see Crisis Management module.
monitoring: Signs of CNS/cardiac toxicity during and after injection

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 25 Local Anesthetics)

infusionPrep: Infusion: 100 mg in 100 mL NS → 1 mg/mL; run 1–4 mg/kg/h (max ~ max dose).
fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS/RL.

mechanism: Potentiates GABA-A receptor mediated chloride conductance.

pharmacokinetics.onset: 1–2 min IV

adult.label: Premedication / sedation
adult.value: IV 0.2 mg/kg titrated (or 1–2 mg IV titrated); oral premedication commonly ~0.5 mg/kg
adult.notes: Reduce in elderly and with opioid co-induction.

pediatric.label: Premedication (oral)
pediatric.value: Commonly ~0.5 mg/kg oral (max varies by age/institution) — confirm institutional protocol

emergency.label: Status epilepticus / sedation
emergency.value: Doses vary by route (IV/IM/buccal/intranasal) — see Crisis Management seizure algorithm

contraindications: Severe respiratory insufficiency without ventilatory support
interactions: Synergistic sedation/respiratory depression with opioids
overdoseManagement: Flumazenil may be considered in select monitored settings; airway/ventilatory support is primary.

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 21 Intravenous Anesthetics; Box 21.2)

infusionPrep: Sedation/infusion: 5 mg in 50 mL NS → 100 mcg/mL; titrate 0.5–2 mg/h.
fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS/RL; compatible with opioids/fentanyl in same line.

mechanism: Competitive antagonist at the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor at the neuromuscular junction.

pharmacokinetics.onset: ED95 ~0.3 mg/kg; 0.6 mg/kg (2×ED95) gives intubating conditions in ~1–2 min; 0.9–1.2 mg/kg faster (approaching suxamethonium speed)
pharmacokinetics.duration: 0.6 mg/kg: clinical duration ~30–40 min; prolonged with higher doses
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic (biliary) and renal excretion; no active metabolites

adult.label: Intubating dose
adult.value: 0.6 mg/kg IV (2×ED95) for rapid intubation; 0.9–1.2 mg/kg IV for faster onset (RSI-style)

infusion.label: Maintenance
infusion.value: 0.075–0.6 mg/kg/h infusion, titrated to twitch response

obese.label: Dosing weight
obese.value: Dose on ideal/lean body weight (volume of distribution scales with TBW; prolonged duration if dosed to TBW)

maximum.label: High-dose RSI
maximum.value: Up to 1.2 mg/kg IV for fastest onset; reversal with sugammadex preferred

contraindications: Personal/family history of malignant hyperthermia (relative — rocuronium itself is not a trigger but context matters)
interactions: Potentiated by volatile agents, aminoglycosides, magnesium; reversed by sugammadex or neostigmine+anticholinergic
overdoseManagement: Ventilate and reverse: sugammadex for deep/moderate block, or neostigmine + glycopyrrolate/atropine once spontaneous recovery evident. Confirm with neuromuscular monitoring.

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 24 Pharmacology of Neuromuscular Blocking Drugs and Antagonists)

rsi.label: RSI paralytic
rsi.notes: Intubating conditions in ~60 s; reverse deep block with sugammadex 16 mg/kg.

infusionPrep: Maintenance infusion: 50 mg in 50 mL NS → 1 mg/mL; run 0.075–0.6 mg/kg/h.
fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS/RL; compatible with common perioperative drugs.

mechanism: Competitive antagonist at the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor at the neuromuscular junction.

pharmacokinetics.onset: ED95 ~0.05 mg/kg; 0.07–0.1 mg/kg gives intubating conditions in ~2–4 min
pharmacokinetics.duration: 0.1 mg/kg: clinical duration ~25–40 min; prolonged in renal/hepatic impairment

adult.label: Intubating dose
adult.value: 0.08–0.1 mg/kg IV (0.1 mg/kg for slightly faster onset; 0.28 mg/kg for rapid sequence if needed)

infusion.label: Maintenance
infusion.value: 1–2 mcg/kg/min infusion, titrated to twitch response

renalAdjustment.label: Renal failure
renalAdjustment.value: Duration prolonged; 0.05–0.14 mg/kg may be unaffected but larger/repeated doses accumulate (active metabolite)

maximum.label: RSI-equivalent
maximum.value: Up to ~0.28 mg/kg IV (4×ED95) for faster onset

interactions: Potentiated by volatile agents, antibiotics (aminoglycosides), magnesium; reversed by neostigmine+anticholinergic or sugammadex
overdoseManagement: Ventilate and reverse with neostigmine + glycopyrrolate/atropine (or sugammadex); confirm with neuromuscular monitoring.

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 24 Pharmacology of Neuromuscular Blocking Drugs and Antagonists)

rsi.label: RSI paralytic (high-dose)
rsi.notes: Slower onset than rocuronium/sux; reverse with neostigmine or sugammadex.

infusionPrep: Maintenance infusion: 10 mg in 100 mL NS → 0.1 mg/mL; run 1–2 mcg/kg/min.
fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS/RL.

drugClass: Selective relaxant binding agent (cyclodextrin) — reverses steroidal NMBDs
mechanism: Encapsulates rocuronium/vecuronium in plasma, lowering free concentration and terminating block.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Reversal of deep rocuronium block achievable within ~3 min at 16 mg/kg

adult.label: Reversal of deep block (2–4 PTCs)
adult.value: 16 mg/kg IV for reversal of deep rocuronium-induced block

emergency.label: Reversal of moderate block (2 twitches)
emergency.notes: 2 mg/kg commonly used for routine reversal at reappearance of 2 twitches.

maximum.label: Repeat dosing
maximum.value: Repeat 16 mg/kg if needed; total doses guided by recurrence of block

contraindications: Use only to reverse aminosteroidal NMBDs (rocuronium/vecuronium)
interactions: Binds rocuronium/vecuronium specifically; not effective for benzylisoquinolines (atracurium/cisatracurium)
sideEffects: Possible masking of oral contraceptive effect briefly
overdoseManagement: No specific antidote; support airway/ventilation and monitor. Re-dose rocuronium if re-paralysis indicated.

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 24 Pharmacology of Neuromuscular Blocking Drugs and Antagonists)

fluidCompatibility: Reconstitute/dilute per label; do not mix with other drugs in same line.

mechanism: Reversibly inhibits acetylcholinesterase, increasing acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction to overcome non-depolarising block.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Onset of reversal ~5–10 min; peak effect ~15–30 min

adult.label: Reversal of non-depolarising block
adult.value: 0.04–0.07 mg/kg IV (commonly 0.043 mg/kg or 2.5–5 mg total) with an anticholinergic
adult.notes: Always co-administer glycopyrrolate/atropine to blunt muscarinic effects.

maximum.label: With glycopyrrolate
maximum.value: Commonly 0.5 mg glycopyrrolate with 2–2.5 mg neostigmine (adult); avoid excessive doses (no benefit, more side effects)

interactions: Synergistic bradycardia with beta-blockers; always pair with anticholinergic
overdoseManagement: Support ventilation; atropine/glycopyrrolate for muscarinic excess; consider quantitative monitoring for residual block.

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 24 Pharmacology of Neuromuscular Blocking Drugs and Antagonists)

fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS; always co-give glycopyrrolate/atropine in same line.

mechanism: Competitive muscarinic antagonism; does not cross the blood–brain barrier (less CNS effect than atropine).

pharmacokinetics.onset: Slower than atropine (~2–3 min IV)

adult.label: With neostigmine (reversal)
adult.value: 0.2–0.4 mg IV paired with neostigmine (commonly 0.5 mg glycopyrrolate with 2–2.5 mg neostigmine)
adult.notes: Used to prevent muscarinic effects of neostigmine.

interactions: Paired with neostigmine for reversal; less CNS penetration than atropine

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 24 Pharmacology of Neuromuscular Blocking Drugs and Antagonists)

fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS; mix with neostigmine for reversal.

mechanism: Agonist at µ-opioid receptors — analgesia, sedation, respiratory depression, MAC reduction.

pharmacokinetics.onset: IV onset ~1–2 min; peak effect ~3–5 min

adult.label: Induction / analgesia bolus
adult.value: 1–2 mcg/kg IV (induction adjunct); titrate to effect

infusion.label: Perioperative infusion
infusion.value: 0.5–3 mcg/kg/h (≈0.005–0.03 mcg/kg/min) as part of balanced anaesthesia; higher for opioid-based techniques
infusion.notes: Often combined with propofol or volatile agent.

maximum.label: High-dose techniques
maximum.value: Cardiac/opioid-based anaesthesia may use 50–100 mcg/kg total — institutional protocol only

interactions: Synergistic respiratory depression with benzodiazepines, propofol, other CNS depressants
CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers alter levels
overdoseManagement: Support airway/ventilation; naloxone titrated IV (watch for pain recurrence and acute withdrawal).

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 22 Opioids)

infusionPrep: Infusion: 500 mcg in 100 mL NS → 5 mcg/mL (or 250 mcg in 50 mL → 5 mcg/mL); run 0.5–3 mcg/kg/h.
fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS/RL; mixes with midazolam/propofol lines.

drugClass: Synthetic phenylpiperidine opioid (µ-agonist); ester-metabolised, ultra-short acting
mechanism: Potent µ-opioid receptor agonist; rapidly hydrolysed by non-specific plasma/tissue esterases.

pharmacokinetics.onset: IV onset ~1 min; peak ~2–4 min
pharmacokinetics.duration: Very short — context-sensitive half-time ~3–6 min regardless of infusion duration

adult.label: Induction bolus
adult.value: 1–2 mcg/kg IV for intubation conditions (4 mcg/kg for rapid intubating conditions)

infusion.label: Maintenance
infusion.value: 0.05–0.3 mcg/kg/min infusion (analgesia 0.025–0.1; surgical 0.1–0.3), titrated to stimulus
infusion.notes: Effect dissipates minutes after stopping — plan postoperative analgesia early.

maximum.label: Upper infusion range
maximum.value: Up to ~1–2 mcg/kg/min in select infused techniques; avoid >1 mcg/kg/min without support

interactions: Profound synergism with propofol/benzodiazepines (resp. depression, hypotension)
Not reversed by naloxone beyond standard — effect ends with metabolism
overdoseManagement: Stop infusion; support airway/ventilation (effect ends within minutes due to esterase metabolism). Naloxone if needed.

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 22 Opioids)

rsi.label: RSI induction
rsi.value: 1–2 mcg/kg IV (4 mcg/kg for rapid intubating conditions)

infusionPrep: Infusion: 2 mg in 50 mL NS → 40 mcg/mL; run 0.05–0.3 mcg/kg/min. Effect ends minutes after stop.
fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS/RL; mix ONLY with water for injection or specific diluents per label.

mechanism: Antagonism of excitatory glutamatergic NMDA receptors; also some opioid-receptor activity (S-enantiomer).

pharmacokinetics.onset: IV 30–60 seconds; IM ~3–5 min
pharmacokinetics.duration: After 2 mg/kg IV: anaesthesia 10–15 min; full orientation 15–30 min

adult.label: IV induction
adult.value: 1–2 mg/kg IV (2 mg/kg gives ~10–15 min anaesthesia)
adult.notes: Children may require slightly higher plasma levels (0.8–4 mcg/mL). IM 4–6 mg/kg alternative.

maximum.label: Analgesic bolus
maximum.value: 0.1–0.5 mg/kg IV boluses for breakthrough analgesia

pregnancy: Used in pregnancy (e.g. trauma/RSI) when indicated; crosses placenta.
contraindications: Increased intracranial pressure without ventilation control (raises CMRO2/CBF/ICP)
interactions: Potentiates CNS depression with other anaesthetics; blunts opioid-induced chest-wall rigidity when combined
overdoseManagement: Supportive airway/ventilation; benzodiazepines for emergence reactions/agitation; no specific antagonist.

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 21 Intravenous Anesthetics)

rsi.label: RSI induction (hemodynamically unstable)
rsi.notes: Preferred when hypotension/shock is a concern.

infusionPrep: Analgesia/sedation: 100–500 mg in 100 mL NS → 1–5 mg/mL; run 0.1–0.5 mg/kg/h.
fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS/RL; stable in infusion.

mechanism: Centrally acting α2-adrenoceptor agonist — sedation, anxiolysis, sympatholysis, minimal respiratory depression.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Sedation within ~15 min of loading infusion
pharmacokinetics.duration: Half-life ~2 h; sedative effect subsides ~1 h after stopping

adult.label: Loading infusion
adult.value: 1 mcg/kg over 10 min (may reduce to 0.5 mcg/kg in adults/elderly or cardiac disease)

infusion.label: Maintenance sedation
infusion.notes: Approved for ICU sedation of initially intubated/mechanically ventilated adults; avoids significant respiratory depression.

maximum.label: Upper maintenance
maximum.value: Commonly not超过 ~0.7–1.4 mcg/kg/h; titrate to sedation goal

interactions: Additive bradycardia/hypotension with other sedatives, opioids, β-blockers, calcium-channel blockers
overdoseManagement: Stop infusion; support airway, fluids, atropine for bradycardia; haemodynamic support.

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 21 Intravenous Anesthetics; ICU sedation)

infusionPrep: Sedation: 200 mcg in 50 mL NS → 4 mcg/mL; load 1 mcg/kg over 10 min, then 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/h.
fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS/RL; do not mix with blood products.

mechanism: Enhances GABA-A receptor-mediated chloride conductance; haemodynamically stable induction.

pharmacokinetics.onset: ~30–60 seconds

adult.label: Induction
adult.value: 0.2–0.6 mg/kg IV (typically 0.3 mg/kg)
adult.notes: Reduce in elderly/sick patients; preferred when haemodynamic stability is critical (e.g. sepsis, cardiac).

maximum.label: Adjunct
maximum.value: 0.1 mg/kg for focal seizures/ECT or brief procedural sedation

interactions: Synergistic CNS depression with opioids/benzodiazepines

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 21 Intravenous Anesthetics)

rsi.label: RSI induction (hemodynamically unstable)
rsi.notes: Preferred when haemodynamic stability is critical (e.g. sepsis, cardiac).

infusionPrep: Sedation: 20 mg in 20 mL NS → 1 mg/mL; titrate to effect.
fluidCompatibility: Compatible with NS/RL.

drugClass: Inhalational volatile anaesthetic (fluorinated methyl isopropyl ether)
mechanism: Potentiates GABA-A and inhibits NMDA receptor function; produces dose-dependent unconsciousness/immobility.
concentrations: Liquid for vapourisation (vaporiser-set %; MAC in adults ~1.8–2.0% at 1 atm, age-dependent)

pharmacokinetics.onset: Rapid uptake (low blood:gas solubility ~0.45); induction/maintenance fast
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic (minor; ~2–5% — compound A formation with CO2 absorbents)

adult.label: Maintenance
adult.value: 0.5–3% inspired (≈0.6–1.5 MAC) titrated to age, comorbidities, co-agents
adult.notes: MAC reduced by ~40% in infants <6 mo; increased in young children; reduced with opioids/benzodiazepines.

pediatric.label: Induction (mask)
pediatric.value: Up to 8% sevoflurane in O2/N2O for inhalational induction in children

contraindications: Avoid in renal impairment with compound-A concern (low-flow debate)
interactions: Potentiates all CNS depressants; MAC reduced by opioids/benzodiazepines
Compound A with desiccated CO2 absorbents — use fresh gas flow ≥2 L/min for low-flow
overdoseManagement: Reduce/increase fresh-gas oxygen, discontinue volatile, support ventilation/circulation; treat MH if triggered.

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 18 Inhaled Anesthetic Uptake, Distribution, Metabolism, and Toxicity; Table 18.1)

fluidCompatibility: Volatile agent — vapourised, not an IV infusion.

mechanism: Potentiates GABA-A and inhibits NMDA receptor function; dose-dependent unconsciousness/immobility.
concentrations: Liquid for vapourisation (vaporiser-set %; MAC in adults ~1.15–1.4% at 1 atm, age-dependent; blood:gas partition coefficient ~1.4)

pharmacokinetics.onset: Moderate uptake (blood:gas ~1.4)

adult.label: Maintenance
adult.value: 0.5–2% inspired (≈0.6–1.5 MAC) titrated to age, comorbidities, co-agents
adult.notes: MAC reduced with opioids/benzodiazepines and with advancing age; elderly MAC ~1.2–1.3%.

interactions: Potentiates all CNS depressants; MAC reduced by opioids/benzodiazepines
sideEffects: Coronary steal (historical concern at very light levels)
overdoseManagement: Reduce/discontinue volatile, support ventilation/circulation; treat MH if triggered.

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 18 Inhaled Anesthetic Uptake, Distribution, Metabolism, and Toxicity; Table 18.1)

fluidCompatibility: Volatile agent — vapourised, not an IV infusion.

drugClass: Inhalational volatile anaesthetic (fluorinated methyl ethyl ether)
mechanism: Potentiates GABA-A and inhibits NMDA receptor function; dose-dependent unconsciousness/immobility.
concentrations: Liquid for vapourisation (requires Tec 6/DED vaporiser; MAC in adults ~6–7% at 1 atm, age-dependent; lowest blood:gas solubility)

pharmacokinetics.onset: Very rapid uptake and wash-in/wash-out (lowest blood:gas solubility)

adult.label: Maintenance
adult.value: 3–10% inspired (≈0.6–1.5 MAC) titrated to age, comorbidities, co-agents
adult.notes: MAC reduced with opioids/benzodiazepines; pungent — poor for inhalational induction in awake adults.

interactions: Potentiates all CNS depressants; MAC reduced by opioids/benzodiazepines
sideEffects: Sympathetic surge with abrupt high concentration
overdoseManagement: Reduce/discontinue volatile, support ventilation/circulation; treat MH if triggered.

source.organization: Miller RD, Gropper MA, Eriksson LI, Fleisher LA, Wiener-Kronish JP, Cohen NH, eds.
source.title: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (Ch. 18 Inhaled Anesthetic Uptake, Distribution, Metabolism, and Toxicity; Table 18.1)

fluidCompatibility: Volatile agent — vapourised, not an IV infusion (requires Tec 6/DED vaporiser).
